services.name: Blotato Engine
services.tagline: One REST API + MCP server to publish to 9 social platforms. Self-hosted, unlimited posts, zero subscription.
services.summary: Blotato sells a unified social media API and MCP server for $29/mo. This engine reproduces the same surface — /v2/posts, /v2/users/me/accounts, /v2/analytics, /v2/dm-automations, /v2/credits, plus a JSON-RPC MCP endpoint — on your own machine. Same request shapes, same tool names, no per-seat billing and no post caps.
highlights: Drop-in REST compatibility with Blotato v2 endpoint shapes
Native JSON-RPC MCP so Claude, Cursor and Hermes get the tools directly
Multi-tenant API keys with per-plan credit quotas and rate limits
Background scheduler dispatches due posts every 15 seconds
Six real platform connectors plus a deterministic mock for testing
Full credit metering wired into every publish call

features.title: Unified publishing
features.body: One POST /v2/posts call targets any connected account. The connector registry resolves the right platform adapter from the account record, so adding a platform never touches your client code.

features.title: Scheduling engine
features.body: Pass an ISO-8601 scheduledTime and the APScheduler worker picks the post up within 15 seconds of its due time. Status moves scheduled to published or failed with the platform error preserved.

features.title: MCP server
features.body: A JSON-RPC endpoint implementing initialize, tools/list and tools/call. Five tools ship by default: list accounts, publish post, get post status, get analytics, check credits.

features.title: Multi-tenant billing
features.body: Every API key carries a plan, a credit balance and an hourly rate limit. Admin keys are unlimited. Client keys stop working the moment credits hit zero, which makes resale trivial.

features.title: Real connectors
features.body: Meta Graph API for Instagram Reels and carousels, X API v2, LinkedIn UGC posts, and Bluesky AT Protocol are implemented directly. Missing credentials fall back to a deterministic mock so the pipeline is always testable.

features.title: Testable by design
features.body: A six-stage end-to-end suite exercises health, account listing, publish, status verification, key minting and MCP tool listing against the real ASGI app.

prereqs: uv package manager (pip also works, uv is faster)

install.title: Clone the repository
install.desc: Grab the monorepo and move into the service directory.

install.title: Install dependencies
install.desc: uv reads pyproject.toml and creates an isolated virtual environment.

install.title: Verify the build
install.desc: Runs the full end-to-end suite. Six checks must pass before you continue.

install.title: Start the server
install.desc: Binds to port 8400. Database and seed accounts are created on first boot.

usage.title: List connected accounts
usage.desc: Every publish call needs an accountId. Fetch the list first; never invent IDs.

usage.title: Publish a post immediately
usage.desc: Omit scheduledTime to publish on the spot. Media must be public URLs.

usage.title: Schedule for later
usage.desc: Add an ISO-8601 timestamp. The scheduler fires within 15 seconds of the due time.

usage.title: Connect an agent over MCP
usage.desc: Drop this into your client config. Any MCP-capable agent gets the publish tools.

usage.title: Mint a key for a paying client
usage.desc: Generates a starter key with 1,000 credits and a 1,800 request/hour ceiling.
usage.code:
uv run python scripts/create_api_key.py \
  --client "Acme Agency" \
  --plan starter \
  --credits 1000

monetization.detail: Master key, unlimited credits, runs on your machine. This is your own engine.
1,000 credits and 1,800 req/hr. Undercuts Blotato's $29 entry tier.
5,000 credits and 3,600 req/hr. Aimed at solo operators running several brands.
Unlimited credits, 10,000 req/hr, white-label docs. For teams reselling social automation.

notes: Instagram and Facebook publishing needs a Meta app with instagram_content_publish and pages_manage_posts approved. Until then the connector returns a mock URL.
X API v2 requires a paid tier for write access. Bearer-only tokens can read but not post.
Media must be publicly reachable URLs. Local files need hosting first; S3 or Cloudflare R2 both work.
The database is SQLite. For multi-instance deployments swap DATABASE_URL to Postgres and run Alembic migrations.
Never expose port 8400 directly. Put it behind Nginx or Caddy with TLS before selling access.

faq.q: Is this the same API as Blotato?
faq.a: The request shapes, endpoint paths and MCP tool names are intentionally identical, so existing n8n flows and agent prompts work unchanged. Blotato's own hosted service is a separate product; this is an independent implementation you run yourself.

faq.q: Can I sell access to it?
faq.a: Yes. Keys carry plans and credit balances, and the API refuses writes once a key is exhausted. Mint keys with scripts/create_api_key.py, collect payment however you like, top up the balance when they renew.
The connector registry falls back to a mock adapter that returns a plausible URL and status. That keeps the full pipeline testable before you have app review approval.
Platform credentials live in the social_accounts table as JSON alongside the account row. For production, encrypt that column or move credentials to a secrets manager.
